Triumph Street Triple 798 RS Goes Live with Moto2-Spec Engine and Lowest Weight Ever
63 photos
Photo: Triumph
Back in October, ahead of the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan, British bike maker Triumph presented the new version of the Street Triple 798. Now, a little more than a month later, we got word of the RS version getting ready to hit the road, bringing with it Moto2 performance levels and the lowest weight in the model's history.
Moto2 is the racing competition meant for young European racers, an intermediate step of Grand Prix motorcycle racing. It's a series Triumph is deeply involved with, as it has been its exclusive engine supplier ever since 2019.
In the time that has passed since, the British tech has proved its worth by travelling a combined 1.24 million miles (two million km) on the championship's circuits all over the world. It didn't travel all that distance in vain, as it has set 89 all-time records and 77 race records, about half of that in the 2025 season.
I just had to mention all of this so you can get a better idea of what to expect from the latest application of this racing technology in the world of civilian riding, more specifically in the Street Triple 798.
As the name of the new bike reveals, the powerplant installed on this bike displaces 798cc. The liquid-cooled triple engine delivers 133 horsepower at 11,500 rpm and 86 Nm of torque at 9,250 rpm (that's ten percent more torque throughout the rev range than before), making the RS the most powerful version of itself yet.
Photo: Triumph There are a lot of new things that have made it into the new engine design. Among them are the larger valves that allow more flow and a higher compression ratio, a redesigned intake for sharper throttle response, and a reworked combustion chamber.
The engine is tied to a new six-speed transmission running the company's shift assist feature, and a fresh exhaust system fitted with twin ground-facing exits. The crankcase is new, while the clutch and primary drive components have been revised. Finally, the injectors are fresh as well.
The motorcycle has been built around an all-new perimeter frame, which includes an aluminum rear subframe and a twin-sided swingarm made of the same material. This final component borrows its design from Moto2, making the two-wheeler look apart.,
The frame is propped on two cast aluminum wheels with five spokes, both sized at 17 inches and shod in Pirelli Diablo Supercorsa V3. The wheel at the front connects to Showa 41 mm upside-down forks with compression and rebound damping and 120 mm wheel travel.
Photo: Triumph At the back, Triumph went for the classic setup and installed an Ohlins piggyback reservoir monoshock that's adjustable for pre-load, compression, and rebound damping. This setup offers 130 mm of travel. Brembo braking hardware is on deck to supply stopping power, completing the setup..
Riders should expect to be seated 836 mm off the ground in the standard configuration, but that can be brought down by 15 mm when going for an optional accessory rear suspension linkage and an extra 30 mm when opting for the accessory seat. If one chooses both these options, they should expect a max seat height of 791 mm.
Triumph didn't look solely to the frame and engine when designing the 2027 Street Triple 798 RS, and expanded its overhaul of the platform to cover smaller components as well, including the 20 mm wider handlebars and the new Bosch seven-inch high-definition TFT touchscreen that is ready to run wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
Described as the most technologically advanced Street Triple to date, it throws into the battle seven riding modes (five preset and two custom) and a wealth of rider assistance systems (including launch control, wheelie control, and traction control, among others).
Photo: Triumph Sitting higher from the ground than its siblings, thanks to an increased ground clearance, the RS got a visual overhaul as well, now being fitted with reimagined twin daylight running lights and three distinct colors for its bodywork: Interstellar Blue, Carnival Red, and Sapphire Black.
I said earlier that the RS is the lightest Street Triple ever, and it's about time I told you what that means. According to the British bike maker, this two-wheeler, with everything discussed above fitted to it, tips the scales at just 403 pounds (183 kg).
Triumph calls the newcomer the herald of a major generational evolution of the Street Triple family, hinting that other models in the range could get at least part of these upgrades in the near future. We will of course keep an eye on that and report back once we know more.
The roadster motorcycle is already listed as available on Triumph's configurators, but it will not actually become available at dealers before the second month of 2027. For the American market, the price for the newcomer has been set at $14,295, making it a proposition few are likely to resist.
